value: mating-signal duet established across an air gap of up to 6 cm between leaves of separate cuttings (no female response at 7 cm); antennal mechanoreceptors not essential for detection; whether the signal is detected as airborne sound or as vibration induced in the receiving leaf is not determined (the authors favour leaf vibration)
method: behavioural tests with live pairs (a calling male and a female on leaves of two separate grapevine cuttings, gap 0.5 to 7 cm; antennae-ablated females against intact males at 5 cm), plus a no-insect transmission test in which a minishaker played a recorded male call into the lower leaf and the upper leaf's velocity was measured at 0.5 to 11 cm; signals recorded with a laser vibrometer
conditions: laboratory-reared virgin adults at least 8 days old, eggs in grapevine canes collected on organic farms at Povo (Trento, northern Italy), hatched and reared in a climate chamber; tests on grapevine (Vitis vinifera) cuttings in the laboratory; gap between upper and lower leaf surface 0.5 to 7 cm; antennae-ablated test used ten pairs (intact males, females without antennae)

source.authors: Eriksson A, Anfora G, Lucchi A, Virant-Doberlet M, Mazzoni V
source.title: Inter-Plant Vibrational Communication in a Leafhopper Insect

quote: Partners established a vibrational duet up to 6 cm gap width between leaves. Ablation of the antennae showed that antennal mechanoreceptors are not essential in detection of mating signals.
note: Crossref lists CC BY 4.0 (unspecified content-version); the repository PDF prints the Creative Commons Attribution License. Results: 'At 7-cm distance between leaves, none of the females responded to MCS' (male calling signal); seven of ten antennae-ablated females responded at a 5 cm gap. Discussion: it was not possible to determine whether signals were detected as air-borne sound or as substrate vibration induced in the leaf; the authors favour substrate vibration. Dominant frequency range of male calling signals 80-300 Hz. Per-gap proportions are in Fig. 1 only, not read. Duets ending in mate location were seen only at the shortest gaps, and call-fly behaviour prevailed at longer gaps (Results, Discussion). Name: Scaphoideus titanus Ball, 1932 is listed under this name in TAXREF (INPN cd_nom 235583); genus Scaphoideus Popenoe, 1885 valid in the 3I Auchenorrhyncha database; GBIF was not used.
